turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): I checked the numbers just now, doctor. Peak flow is two hundred and eighty, and on his card the best is four hundred and fifty. Pulse is one hundred and four, saturation ninety-six percent, respiratory rate twenty-two, temperature thirty-six point eight.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. What brought you?
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, after the cold he is wheezing so badly. The whistle is there from ten days, and last night he was feverish, quite hot to touch.
[SEG0004] person_4 (PATIENT): Ma, enough, it is not ten days. The cold came first, and the wheeze started four days back only. I did not have any fever, I am just tired. Can we not drag this.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright, wheeze somewhere between four and ten days. Cough?
[SEG0006] person_4 (PATIENT): Yes, cough. It is dry, well, actually mostly dry. More in the night, it wakes me.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Short of breath?
[SEG0008] person_4 (PATIENT): On the stairs, yes. Sitting, it is only this tight feeling in the chest.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Chest pain?
[SEG0010] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Phlegm? Any blood?
[SEG0012] person_4 (PATIENT): No phlegm. No blood.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Asthma from before?
[SEG0014] person_4 (PATIENT): Since childhood only. It never really went.
[SEG0015] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He has the blue inhaler and the brown one, but he confuses them. When the breathing is bad he pumps the brown one, I have seen it.
[SEG0016] person_4 (PATIENT): Not every time, Ma. I know the blue one is the reliever. I use it maybe five, six times a day, two puffs. The brown one I am taking most mornings and nights.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Blue is salbutamol, one hundred microgram. Brown is beclomethasone, two puffs twice daily. You are mixing them.
[SEG0018] person_4 (PATIENT): Sometimes I pick the wrong pump, yes. I am not doing it for fun. Um, my head is pounding, I hardly slept, can we hurry.
[SEG0019] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The brown inhaler counter is almost the same as last month. He is missing doses, doctor, whatever he says.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0021] person_4 (PATIENT): No. I have never smoked.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any medicine allergy?
[SEG0023] person_4 (PATIENT): Nothing. No allergies.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me listen. There is wheeze on both sides of the chest. No crackles. Heart sounds are normal.
[SEG0025] person_4 (PATIENT): Oh, the runny nose has settled. Sore throat was only for two days, that also went.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Working impression, this is an acute asthma flare after that viral cold. Peak flow is well below his best.
[SEG0027] person_1 (NURSE): You want a nebuliser and a repeat peak flow?
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not now. I am starting prednisolone tablets, forty milligram, once every morning, for five days. Take it with food, and stop after five days, no taper.
[SEG0029] person_4 (PATIENT): Five days of tablets and then leave it. Fine.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Blue inhaler when you wheeze, two puffs. Brown inhaler, two puffs morning and night, every day. Do not swap them.
[SEG0031] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I will keep the brown one and give it to him myself.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): If you cannot finish a sentence, or the breathing turns much worse, go to emergency. Otherwise I will see you in one week.
[SEG0033] person_4 (PATIENT): One week, okay. I just want to lie down. My college assignment is still not written, which is not your problem, sorry.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anyone at home with asthma?
[SEG0035] person_4 (PATIENT): My father has it.
[SEG0036] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His father, yes, he is also on inhalers.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. Collect the prescription outside and go home.

features: relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.

spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.
